nodes.author: Tor Harald Sandve
nodes.norm_label: discrete fracture matrix (dfm) module for mrst

nodes.label: Control Volume Discretization of Fractured Media
nodes.rationale: Fractures are represented as lower-dimensional objects but still as cells in the computational grid, enabling control volume flux approximations (TPFA and MPFA) while maintaining geometric conformity. This avoids explicit coupling terms between fracture and matrix by embedding fractures as faces/edges in the grid.
nodes.norm_label: control volume discretization of fractured media

nodes.label: Multi-Point Flux Approximation (MPFA)
nodes.rationale: MPFA is used over TPFA for improved accuracy on non-K-orthogonal grids, but has known limitations: does not handle pyramids in 3D, and is barely tested with gravity. TPFA is simpler and more robust for gravity problems.

nodes.label: Lower-Dimensional Fracture Representation
nodes.rationale: Fractures are modeled as lower-dimensional objects (faces/edges in the grid rather than volumetric cells) to reduce computational cost while preserving the physical role of fractures as preferential flow paths.

nodes.label: Conforming Grid for Fracture Discretization
nodes.source_location: page 1, Lessons learned in gridding of fractures
nodes.rationale: Conforming grids ensure fractures are represented as edges in the grid mesh, which is critical for accuracy but non-trivial to generate. Relaxed fracture positioning with snapping to an underlying grid is a practical compromise to improve cell quality near fractures.

nodes.label: Fracture Face and Cell Tagging System (G.faces.tags, G.cells.tags)
nodes.rationale: Tags are essential for identifying fracture faces (tag > 0) and hybrid cells in transmissibility computations. The current single-tag system is a known limitation; a matrix-based tagging (G.faces.tags as matrix, G.faces.tagcols as string identifiers) is recommended for multi-family fracture networks.
nodes.norm_label: fracture face and cell tagging system (g.faces.tags, g.cells.tags)

nodes.label: MRST Core Files Modified with _DFM Suffix
nodes.rationale: Modified MRST core transport solvers are suffixed _DFM to distinguish them from originals and to add fracture transport support. This is a static fork of MRST 2011a, meaning upstream changes to core functions are not reflected.
